node.acceptance_condition: At least 3 distinct arguments, each with a one-sentence claim and 2–4 sentences of plain-language support; arguments must be distinct (not restatements), intellectually honest, and free of invented statistics or fake citations.
node.expected_contribution: The prosecution case the essay's thesis must absorb and answer.
node.objective: Assemble the strongest honest version of the prosecution: the argument that AI-generated art is kitsch by default. Deliver 3–4 distinct arguments (for example: training on existing imagery averages taste toward the already-approved; the prompt-and-select workflow delivers sentiment on demand without risk; the visible flood of formulaic AI 'slop' online; optimization for engagement rewards instant appeal). State each argument as a claim plus 2–4 sentences of support, steelmanned — the version a thoughtful critic would actually make.
node.rationale: D3 requires a defended thesis, and a thesis earns its nuance by confronting the strongest case against its subject; this child supplies that case.
